coachingPoints: Two feet = two powers: balance and the ability to absorb contact without traveling.
Seek the defender's body, not their arms — chest-to-chest contact is your foul.
Ball never drops below the waist in traffic — that's where strips happen.
Finish with a soft touch, not a slam attempt; power is in the setup, finesse in the finish.
Chin the ball on the catch if you receive it in the paint — elbows out, pivots ready.
commonMistakes: Jumping into the defender off one foot and falling away — no balance, no call.
Bringing the ball down low to 'load up' — it gets stripped; keep it high.
Finishing on the defender's side instead of extending away from the contact.
Stopping the motion when bumped — play through; a stopped finish is just a miss.
description: Stop on two feet, rip the ball through contact, and finish strong at the rim — the big man's layup.
gameSituations: Post catches where the defender bodied you — jump stop, power up through the chest.
Offensive rebounds — gather with two feet and go back up strong instead of a soft tip.
Drives into a set help defender — stop early, absorb, finish or draw the and-one.

howTo.detail: Attack the lower paint with the ball on your outside hip. You want the defender's chest or shoulder contact, not a swipe at the ball.
howTo.title: Drive into the contact zone

howTo.detail: Plant both feet at the same time — feet slightly wider than shoulders, knees bent. Your base must be set before the bump arrives, not after.
howTo.title: Jump stop into contact

howTo.detail: Bring the ball from low to high in a straight, strong line — 'rip it through' the contact. Keep elbows tight and the ball above your waist at all times.
howTo.title: Rip the ball up strong

howTo.detail: Let your legs take the bump, then explode upward off both feet. Finish with the hand away from the defender, using the board for a soft, high-percentage touch.
howTo.title: Absorb and go up

howTo.detail: Keep your shooting motion natural and continuous through the hit. Officials call fouls on players finishing strong in balance — flailing or throwing the ball gets nothing.
howTo.title: Sell the foul

title: Power Finish
whatIsIt: A power finish is a two-foot stop at the rim followed by an aggressive, balanced finish — usually with the ball brought up strong through contact. It's the go-to finish for bigs and strong drivers who meet resistance in the paint.

Instead of floating around contact, you embrace it: stop on two feet, absorb the bump with your lower body, and power up. The two-foot base makes you harder to move and more likely to draw the and-one.
whyItMatters: Referees reward players who play through contact in balance. A power finish turns defensive physicality into fouls and three-point plays, while finesse finishes under the same contact often just miss. It's also simply more reliable — two feet, one bump absorbed, one clean look.
